specDepartures.spec: "two files that launcher writes on the daemon's own disk … cannot be written into a pod at all, because a launch carries a command line, an environment and its secrets and nothing else".
specDepartures.plan: A launch also carries files: the plan delivers the Claude worker's mcp.json through shimwire.LauncherStart.Files, which the in-pod launcher writes 0600 into the generation's private directory.
specDepartures.evidence: packages/daemon/internal/shimwire/frames.go:179-186 declares Files; packages/daemon/internal/launcher/launcher.go:371-412 writes each entry O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW at 0600 into the 0700 generation directory and removes it when the generation ends; packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/launcher.go:414-426 is where launcherCommand already builds that map from the claim's secrets and boot token.

specDepartures.spec: "What is not in scope is the operator's model route, which Legion does not hold for any harness: a pod's provider key already reaches whatever the worker runs, through the environment the shim gives the child (shim/shim.go:380)."
specDepartures.plan: The plan keeps that scope — no new configuration key and no Legion-held credential — but records that the sentence holds only through provider_keys, and writes the operator's duty into the documents: provider_keys for the Anthropic credential and the non-credential names ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and ANTHROPIC_MODEL in runtime.kubernetes.pod.env.
specDepartures.evidence: The documented pod route is Oh My Pi's profile configuration — deploy/kubernetes/operator-route/pod.yml mounts models.yml into Oh My Pi's profile and names the overlay in PI_CONFIG_FILES — and Claude Code reads none of it; runtime.kubernetes.pod.env refuses a credential-shaped name (packages/daemon/internal/config/kubernetes.go:665-671), so the key can only arrive through provider_keys, which the shim exports into the child's environment (shim/shim.go:379-380, shim/config.go:69-100). The planner measured that Claude Code reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and ANTHROPIC_MODEL from its environment. The consequence the spec does not state is that a provider key reaches every role's child, Oh My Pi's included, which is why the tmux proof's guard against ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in an agent's environment does not carry over to a pod.

outcome.scope: A deployment that runs Claude Code roles under Kubernetes must set provider_keys and two pod.env names it does not set today; the plan adds that to docs/kubernetes.md and deploy/kubernetes/daemon/legion.yaml.example rather than adding a Legion configuration key.

risks: The bridge needs passwordless sudo on the devbox (present; refused by name otherwise).
Network policy for five ports from issue pods to a scratch Service is unmeasured on this cluster for this script.
deploy/kubernetes/operator-route/pod-key-file.yml has not driven a daemon-launched pod on this cluster before.
The devbox agent is a separate session; a dispatch ask replaces it if it stops answering.
The runtime token must outlive the run.

findings.finding: 1 (blocking) — The daemon is not the only devbox process that dials the pod-facing URLs: the scratch Envoy listener dials NATS, scratch Dispatch dials NATS and the listener, and the script's readiness curls and lib/workflow.sh Dispatch calls dial dispatch_base; legion.yaml's dispatch_url and the script's dispatch_base are one variable today.
findings.answer: G2: the script's one host becomes two names, host (pod-facing: advertise_host, daemon_url, envoy_url, nats_urls, a new pod_dispatch_url written as dispatch_url, DISPATCH_SERVER_URL, the pod endpoint assertions) and bind_host (devbox-local: every bind, the listener's and Dispatch's outbound NATS/Envoy URLs, dispatch_base, every readiness curl), with a table assigning each use. The daemon's own Envoy dial is confirmed (workflow.go:477, notify.go:97-106).

findings.finding: 2 (blocking) — The private-hosts namespace wrapper was unverified on the devbox, and must keep the daemon's uid, D-Bus/secrets access, recorded pid and the wildcard bind.
findings.answer: Measured on the devbox: unprivileged user namespaces are refused by AppArmor (bwrap and unshare --user both fail at the uid map); passwordless sudo works. G3 therefore uses sudo -n unshare --mount, setpriv back to the devbox user with its groups, an explicit environment, and a pidfile written by the exec chain's shell so daemon_pid is the daemon's own; prerequisites probe the wrapper (ids, getent, /etc/hosts sha256 unchanged) and refuse by name. bind: 0.0.0.0 stays (config/kubernetes.go:1456-1459).

findings.finding: 3 (blocking) — start_daemon re-runs ports_free over all five ports after the run's own NATS, listener and Dispatch already hold three of them, so every run would stop at the daemon's boot.
findings.answer: G6: start_daemon checks only the daemon API and worker-stream ports; the five-port check stays in prerequisites.

findings.finding: 4 (blocking) — The bridge watchdog calls stage4a's kill_harness before kill -TERM $$; the sandbox script defines none, and under errexit the watchdog would die before signalling.
findings.answer: G4 makes kill_harness part of the library's documented caller contract; G5 defines it in the sandbox script as a TERM to the daemon's pid from $work/daemon.pid, without sourcing lib/teardown.sh.

findings.finding: 5 (blocking) — namespace-rig's teardown deletes no standalone Pod or Service, so the bridge must be stopped explicitly and before namespace_clean; bridge creation must follow the before-snapshot.
findings.answer: G5: begin bridge right after begin snapshot and before operator-route; cleanup adds bridge_stop after the transcripts and the daemon stop and before the scratch services, the process sweep, teardown and namespace_clean; bridge_stop is safe after a partial start.

findings.finding: 6 (blocking) — The devbox's restricted kubeconfig does not parse, and a token alone is not a kubeconfig; the operator context must not stand in for the runtime identity.
findings.answer: G7: the runtime kubeconfig stays an operator input; the README's GKE example gains the recipe (operator context's server and CA, a token from kubectl create token legion-daemon with a duration longer than the run, auth can-i --list as the identity check); the devbox agent builds it outside the repository and leaves ~/.kube/legion-daemon-production alone.

findings.finding: 7 (blocking) — The run needs non-script inputs: storage class, five free ports, routes, Claude model, contexts, and an image whose provenance matches the proof head.
findings.answer: Step 7 lists every non-secret input the implementer gives the devbox agent, and takes the image from the pull request's latest successful Worker Image run only when jj diff over worker-image.yaml's paths list between that run's commit and the proof head is empty, recording run id, digest and revision label.

findings.finding: 8 (blocking) — The evidence protocol for a tester and reviewer who cannot run the proofs was missing, and one delegated run must not stand for two.
findings.answer: Steps 7 and 8: the implementer's runs (R1) and the tester's own runs (R2) are separate devbox runs; each run's transcript.log (and the sandbox's namespace snapshots) is uploaded to the Dispatch issue; the E2E lines name command shape, head, PASS line, exit status after cleanup, artifact references and a negative control; the reviewer reviews the new head as a new round.

findings.finding: 9 (blocking) — Making bridge_start variadic must cover every port-dependent part and keep stage4a's two-port behaviour; executable regressions were asked for.
findings.answer: G4 names every port-dependent part (containerPorts, Service ports, free-port exclusion, reverse forwards, readiness lines) and keeps stage4a's call unchanged; C5 is checked by reading the diff against the two-port original and bash -n, and the sandbox run drives the five-port path live. No stub-driven test of the library is added: it would test kubectl/chisel wiring, which the repository's test rules exclude.

findings.finding: 10 (blocking) — The key-file installer requires its --key-dir removed on every exit; the tmux script's cleanup does not do that.
findings.answer: G1 copies stage3-devbox-workflow.sh:124-128's unconditional rm -rf "$work/model-gateway-key" as the first line of cleanup, keeping the call record under $evidence/model-gateway.

findings.finding: 11 (non-blocking) — Documentation of the sandbox's new input, the bridge library's contract and the port-admission note was missing; one daemon citation pointed at the tmux runtime.
findings.answer: G8 lists every document; the plan cites internal/daemon/kubernetes.go:330-334 for the sandbox's URL forwarding; no CHANGELOG (no package owns scripts/e2e); no private name in the tree or pull request text.

implement: legion-worker: the implementer's rules here — references/pr-body.md (the proof and the PR body; the production-like surfaces reachable from a pod are the pinned Oh My Pi binary, the real MCP server over stdio, the real Claude Code binary against stand-ins, and `go test ./...`), references/default-branch-check.md before each push, references/cleanup-deletion.md for the Go cut of claudebridge/stall.go and for the tmux-only prose this change makes false, references/conflicts-and-rewrites.md only on a conflict.

ce-simplify-code: the simplify pass over the settled diff. Two copies are the risk this change exists to avoid: the phase-stall machine (already one, in @legion/pi-shared) and the Claude launch shapes, which the plan puts in packages/daemon/internal/claudelaunch for both runtimes to import.
dispatch-first: search before any Dispatch write; a problem outside this issue is a dispatch ask, never an issue the implementer files (skill://legion-worker/references/findings.md).
test: legion-worker: references/pr-body.md — the tester drives the application and reads CI for everything static. The pod-runnable surfaces are `go test ./...` in packages/daemon, `bun test` in pi-legion, pi-shared and claude-envoy, the pinned Oh My Pi real-binary test, and the real Claude Code probe; the two live proofs (scripts/e2e/claude-backend-tmux.sh and the new scripts/e2e/claude-backend-sandbox.sh) need a devbox and a cluster, as every live proof in this repository does, and the tester records that rather than claiming them.
dispatch-first: search before any Dispatch write; findings outside this issue are asks.
review: legion-worker: references/review-threads.md for one disposition reply and one resolution per thread, references/merge-gate.md for the order of the round.
ce-simplify-code: the reviewer judges whether the Claude launch really has one definition rather than two, and whether the pod path grew a backend seam rather than a second runtime.
dispatch-first: search before any Dispatch write; findings outside this issue are asks.

findings.finding: F1 — the spec calls the model route out of scope on the strength of shim.go:380, but the documented pod route (deploy/kubernetes/operator-route/) is Oh My Pi's profile configuration, which Claude Code reads none of; the only variable route is provider_keys through the shim, and pod.env refuses a credential-shaped name.
findings.answer: D20: no new Legion surface. A deployment that runs Claude Code roles sets provider_keys for the Anthropic credential (the shim exports it into the child's environment) and the non-credential names ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and ANTHROPIC_MODEL in runtime.kubernetes.pod.env; the planner measured that Claude Code reads all three from its environment. The two consequences — the key reaching every role's child, and Oh My Pi's model configuration reaching Claude Code not at all — are written into the documents, and the departure is recorded for the architect.

findings.finding: F2 — the daemon API contract is defined as the pane and pod environment a worker reads, and this work adds four LEGION_STALL_* variables under both runtimes and three CLAUDE_* variables in a pod; the spec never mentions the contract.
findings.answer: D25: one bump to 36, in the same commit as the variables, with contracts/fixtures/daemon-api/version.json, pi-legion's and claude-envoy's legion.daemonApiVersion and pi-legion's daemon-api-version test; the boot gate then holds the daemon and the image's plugins together.

findings.finding: F3 — the earlier K10 named workerSpawnSpec for both edits, but the stale-plugin decision is in stalePluginInstall (reached from SpawnSpec, which also covers the controller), and workerSpawnSpec replaces spec.Env with the git identity's map rather than merging into it.
findings.answer: D26: the four variables are merged into spec.Env after `spec.Env = id.Env()`, and the Claude branch is inside stalePluginInstall, which gains the claim's backend from the resolver launchBackend uses.

findings.finding: F4 — a Backend field on shimwire.LauncherStart buys nothing the child's environment does not already decide, and would be ignored silently by an image whose launcher predates it.
findings.answer: D21: no wire field. A Claude pod is simply not told OMP_SESSION_STORAGE and OMP_SESSION_SQL_DSN_FILE, so the in-pod launcher takes its file branch and stats the transcript.

findings.finding: F5 — the claim's session for a Claude worker travels through four more code points than the spec names: what claude-envoy registers, validateSessionPath, SessionOnVolume with `legion sessions import`, and the store's IssueHasSessions.
findings.answer: D21 and D22 name each: the transcript under the pod's own Claude directory, a backend-aware validateSessionPath whose refusal names a backend change, `--resume <uuid>` in the argv, a refusal with a line of its own from `legion sessions import`, and expectVolume losing its sessionsInDatabase term for a Claude claim.

findings.finding: F6 — under Kubernetes nothing resolves claude, bun or the plugin directory: the three LEGION_CLAUDE_*/LEGION_BUN_PATH reads are tmux's boot alone.
findings.answer: D16: the pod's paths are image constants beside defaultAgent and join imageOwnedPaths so an operator mount cannot hide them; claudelaunch holds the shapes and not the paths, and docs/deployment.md's 'boot resolves three things' becomes tmux's boot alone.

findings.finding: F7 — a Claude-only pod variable makes the runtimeOwned pinning test red either way: in the list, the test's two specs do not set it; out of it, a spec or an operator could override the claim's own config directory.
findings.answer: D19: the three names join runtimeOwned and the test gains a Claude worker spec beside its Oh My Pi and controller ones; the operator's own CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY stays settable.

findings.finding: F8 — ten more Go tests and eight pod goldens pin the pod's command line, environment, mounts, refusals and plugin install.
findings.answer: B8 lists them by file and line, and takes a ninth golden — a Claude worker pod — rather than editing the eight, so an Oh My Pi pod keeps proving it is unchanged.

findings.finding: F9 — a SiteImage capability row makes Claude Code mandatory in every image and moves the contracts fixture, the probe goldens and the docs; and nothing yet holds claude-envoy's declared contract to the daemon's.
findings.answer: D24 accepts the first and names it as risk 2, and gives the probe's Claude lane the second: it holds packages/claude-envoy's legion.daemonApiVersion to the daemon's contract as the pod lane holds pi-legion's.

findings.finding: F10 — the image workflow's paths allowlist covers only packages/claude-envoy/package.json, and check-image-trigger-paths.sh fails the lint job for a COPY it does not cover.
findings.answer: B2: packages/claude-envoy/** joins the allowlist with the new lockfile directory; the plan also records that the image's Bun ARG and .bun-version are already equal and kept so by check-bun-version.sh, which is what lets `bun run check-dist` run inside the build.

findings.finding: F11 — nothing in a pod makes the claim's Claude directory, and the shim's directory-making list is pinned.
findings.answer: D19: the generation's start script makes it with one mkdir before the exec, which is the wrapper that already exists for installing launches and operator setup; the shim's pinned list is left alone.

findings.finding: F12 — the launcher's Files map is a legitimate home for a non-secret file, with two conditions.
findings.answer: D18 carries both: the entry is added in launcherCommand and never through spec.Secrets, and the argv names it as the generation directory's own file so a repeated start with the same id carries an unchanged payload.

findings.finding: F13 — the pod baseline is Oh My Pi-shaped and would wrap a Claude child, including the turn-scoping overlay quiescence depends on.
findings.answer: D19: --pod-safety stays, because its scratch directories and state home are harness-neutral and its Oh My Pi variables are inert for a child that reads none of them; the two CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_* variables are named as Claude Code's analogue of the overlay rather than as a nicety.

findings.finding: F14 — K6's `--check-config` half had no home, and nothing there prints anything about a per-launch plugin decision today.
findings.answer: D23: the existing plugin-pair line gains one sentence naming each Claude-backed role and saying its plugin comes from the image; a Claude claim with a stale recorded contract still relaunches, and the image probe is what refuses a wrong plugin.

findings.finding: F15 — a Claude worker in a pod is told LEGION_WORKSPACE_RECREATED and nothing reads it; the only consumer is the Oh My Pi plugin.
findings.answer: Out of scope, named as risk 5 and reported to the architect: a Claude worker resumed into a recreated workspace is not told so.

findings.finding: F16 — acceptance bullet 1's 'a live proof drives one on the cluster' reads as either a throwaway kind cluster or a real one, with different costs, locking and credential paths.
findings.answer: D27: a new devbox script against a real cluster by context with a digest-pinned image, carrying the tmux proof's scratch rig and its five assertions; the kind library is named as the iteration path, and the recorded run that satisfies acceptance is the cluster one.

findings.finding: F17 — every pod proof needs a published image built from the branch head, and the image gate is the thing being changed.
findings.answer: D27 and risk 1: the proof pins the pull-request build's digest, and B2 and B3 land together so the image answers the probe it ships; a build that cannot be produced is a report to the architect, not a line marked proven.

findings.finding: F18 — nine places state the tmux-only rule and one pinned refusal message.
findings.answer: D28 lists each document and B11 takes the refusals and their tests last.

findings.finding: F19 — the issue volume, roleStateHome and the one-line expectVolume change hold as assumed.
findings.answer: Recorded; D19 and D22 rely on it.

findings.finding: F20 — `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` with a fresh CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR under a non-root uid is unmeasured.
findings.answer: Risk 4: the real-binary Claude probe adds that flag set and a fresh directory under the pod's own uid, so the pod lane is measured before the cluster proof depends on it.

findings.finding: F21 — the spec's sentence that a launch carries 'a command line, an environment and its secrets and nothing else' overstates the constraint; it also carries files.
findings.answer: Departure 1 records the correction, which is what D18 uses.

findings.finding: F22 — the acceptance list holds thirteen bullets, not twelve, and its second uses `*` where the others use `-`.
findings.answer: Departure 5 and §3: the plan maps all thirteen and reads the last as the evidence clause of the other twelve; the owner decides whether it is a criterion of its own.

findings.answer: §3 maps all thirteen to a suite and a command, names the four suites that run in a pod and the two live proofs that do not, and says the implementer's own proof is the pod-runnable four.
